conclusion: The current gfx1151 GGUF deficit is shape- and family-specific, not a blanket llama.cpp implementation advantage. At 4K, exact GDN recurrence and linear-attention convolution account for the dominant measured excess; the long-token convolution schedule is the highest-confidence exact-plausible transfer. llama.cpp's GDN reduction tree is faster but conflicts with hipEngine's stronger exact trajectory contract. hipEngine already wins the matched selected-Q4, selected-Q5, and full-attention family buckets, so those are not port targets.

gpf5a_profile_delta.note: These are separately profiled diagnostic runs, not a same-process causal A/B. The clean focused GPF-5A gates remain the causal evidence.

source_findings.gdn: llama.cpp keeps a state-column shard in registers across the serial token loop and uses wave reductions. hipEngine's exact default keeps a 128x32 state tile in LDS and preserves canonical scalar contraction order. The prior register/tree replication was fast but failed the exact trajectory gate, so the source schedule is evidence for algorithm research, not a direct port.
source_findings.linear_attn_conv: llama.cpp's long-token kernel tiles 32 tokens by 128 channels into shared memory and fuses SiLU. hipEngine maps one thread to each token/channel output, reads its four-value window from global memory, and updates state in a second launch. This schedule is independently testable without changing convolution math.
source_findings.quantized_matmul: llama.cpp quantizes activations to a bank-conflict-aware Q8_1 MMQ layout, stages weight and activation tiles in shared memory, and shape-selects MMQ tile width. hipEngine's replacement T16 layouts already beat llama.cpp in Q4/Q5; only dense Q8 remains slower after GPF-5A.
source_findings.moe_router: llama.cpp fuses softmax/top-k/get-rows and routes MUL_MAT_ID through sorted MMVQ/MMQ. hipEngine's separate select is small at 4K; the F32 router-logits matrix kernel owns most of the router bucket, so matrix-kernel screening precedes top-k fusion.
source_findings.attention: llama.cpp has architecture/shape-aware vector, tile, WMMA, and MMA FlashAttention selection. hipEngine AOTriton is already faster in the complete 512/4K family traces, so no short/mid attention port is selected.
source_findings.graph_dispatch: llama.cpp supports graph-level operator fusion, concurrent events, and HIP graph replay. It nevertheless launches more traced kernels than hipEngine at both measured prefill shapes, so generic launch-count work is not the current prefill blocker.
source_findings.memory: llama.cpp's graph allocator aliases eligible parent buffers and frees intermediates at their last consumer. hipEngine's bulk-prefill scratch allocates all named intermediates concurrently. Cross-engine peak scopes differ, so this is a design opportunity rather than a measured allocator-efficiency claim.

explicit_non_targets: Do not replace selected Q4/Q5 with generic llama.cpp MMQ: hipEngine's measured families are already faster.
Do not replace short/mid AOTriton with llama.cpp FlashAttention: hipEngine's measured attention family is already faster.
Do not re-enable GPF-4 isolated AOTriton queues by default: the final stability gate remains rejected.
Do not port llama.cpp's GDN wave-reduction tree under the exact/default name: it changes contraction order and failed hipEngine's trajectory contract.
Do not prioritize generic graph/dispatch reduction for prefill: llama.cpp has more measured dispatches and the gap is kernel-family wall.
